clue.text: I? Insane, mad and moronic?

indicators.note: something mad is deranged, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks, aghast, whether they themselves are insane and foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine literally means like an ass, so stupid or foolish behaviour, a close synonym of moronic.

clue.text: Push bad privatisation

parts.note: to push goods is to sell them hard
food that is off has gone bad

explanation.surface: A campaign against a poorly judged sale of state industries.
explanation.definitionFit: A sell-off is the sale of a nationally owned business to private investors, which is privatisation.

clue.text: Dark, misshapen thing

indicators.note: misshapen means deformed out of its proper form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shadowy, deformed creature from a horror film.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the period of darkness between sunset and sunrise; 'dark' as a noun names the same time.

clue.text: Horrible snot starts to run in left part of nose

indicators.note: something horrible is in a terrible state, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, which alone are kept

parts.note: opening letters of run and in
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A runny nose: unpleasant mucus starts dripping on the left side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run in' looks like part of the picture, but its two words each give a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostril is one of the two external openings of the nose, so literally a part of it.

clue.text: Said to be hiding before first of spectacular robberies

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the phrase for hiding is wanted as heard rather than as written

parts.note: someone holed up is hiding; the phrase sounds like this spelling

indicators.note: first of asks for only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: opening letter of spectacular

explanation.surface: A tale of spectacular robberies carried out by gangs lying low beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: Holed up, meaning hiding, is pronounced like HOLD UP; 'before' places it ahead of the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A hold-up is an armed robbery, typically of a bank or vehicle, so the plural matches robberies.

clue.text: Bond villain's bit of casual work

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Goldfinger's hat-throwing henchman in the James Bond story
second meaning: a small occasional task, often domestic

explanation.surface: A Bond baddie takes on a little casual employment.
explanation.definitionFit: The henchman with the steel-rimmed bowler shares a name with a small piece of handyman labour.

clue.text: Perhaps Saddam Hussain, Milosevic and Castro mingled with leaders of international trade delegation

indicators.note: mingled means mixed together, so the letters are stirred up and recombined

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so the opening letters of the next words are kept

parts.note: opening letters of international, trade and delegation

explanation.surface: Notorious strongmen attend an international trade meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Castro looks like the end of the list of tyrants, but it is the anagram fodder; the list ends at Milosevic.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddam Hussein of Iraq and Slobodan Milosevic of Serbia were both autocratic rulers holding absolute power.

clue.text: Plan piece of school work

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a planned undertaking or scheme
second meaning: an extended assignment a pupil researches

explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both a scheme being worked out and a topic study set for pupils at school.

clue.text: Anyhow, in brief, guilt's a waste of time

definitions.note: the answer is a gerund, a noun naming the activity

indicators.note: anyhow means in a careless, haphazard way, so the letters land in any order

parts.note: the letters as written, punctuation dropped

explanation.surface: A brisk dismissal: put shortly, feeling guilty achieves nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Filibustering is making long speeches to delay a vote in a legislature, deliberately wasting time.

clue.text: Beginning to pull, drag and push

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: opening letter of pull
to lug is to drag something heavy

explanation.surface: Instructions for moving something heavy: pull, drag and push.
explanation.definitionFit: To plug a product is to promote or publicise it insistently, the marketing sense of push.

clue.text: Drive to emasculate Alastair Campbell, perhaps

parts.note: a spin is a short drive in a car
to doctor an animal is to castrate it

explanation.surface: A desire to cut the powerful press chief Alastair Campbell down to size.
explanation.walkthrough: Alastair Campbell was Tony Blair's press secretary and communications director, famous for managing the news.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin doctor puts a favourable slant on news for politicians, and Campbell is the best-known British example.

clue.text: Cad's outrageous retort

indicators.note: outrageous suggests something wildly out of order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A scoundrel makes a shocking reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotter and cad are both dated British terms for a man who behaves dishonourably, especially towards women.

clue.text: I'd love subsequently to become a passionate admirer

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
subsequently means afterwards

explanation.surface: Someone hoping to become a devoted fan at some later date.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater worships idols, and by extension is someone who adores a person or thing excessively.

clue.text: Smutty, somewhat offensive and blue, perhaps

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the following word is used, here its opening letters

parts.note: the first three letters of offensive
blue is an example of a colour

explanation.surface: Describing a rude joke as dirty, a bit offensive and risqué.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like a further synonym for smutty, but here it is just a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: An off-colour joke is slightly indecent or in poor taste, the same idea as smutty humour.

clue.text: Vexed by loud anger in heated exchange

parts.note: cross means annoyed
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
ire is a literary word for anger

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed by shouted fury in a bitter argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loud' is not a homophone signal here; it is the musical abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossfire is figuratively a sharp, rapid exchange of hostile remarks, like gunfire from opposing sides.

clue.text: Steals instruments, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the word for the instruments is taken by pronunciation

parts.note: lutes are plucked stringed instruments

explanation.surface: A thief makes off with musical instruments, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: To loot is to plunder or rob, especially during a riot, a vivid synonym for steals.

clue.text: Reconstructed Roman villa

indicators.note: something reconstructed is put together again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Archaeologists have rebuilt an ancient Roman country house.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor is a large country house with lands, as a villa was in Roman times.

clue.text: Topless partying causes excitement!

indicators.note: in a down answer the top is the first letter, so topless means that letter is removed

parts.note: a carousal is a noisy, drunken party or revelry

explanation.surface: A cheeky tabloid line about bare-chested revellers causing a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: Arousal is a state of being stirred up or stimulated, emotionally or physically, which is excitement.

clue.text: Senior politician sets out to work

parts.note: to set out an argument is to state it
to man a machine or post is to work it

explanation.surface: An elder statesman of a party briefs colleagues and gets down to business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sets out' tempts an anagram of SETS, but it is a single verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A statesman is an experienced, respected political leader, so a senior politician.

clue.text: Ruin poor Ted in crash

indicators.note: in a crash things are smashed apart, so the letters end up jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Unlucky Ted is wrecked in a car accident.
explanation.definitionFit: To torpedo a plan is to wreck or destroy it suddenly, a figurative sense matching ruin as a verb.

clue.text: A terrible crime initially appalled the US

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: terrible means dreadfully bad, so the word is knocked out of shape

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: opening letter of appalled

explanation.surface: A dreadful atrocity shocked the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: America is the everyday name for the United States, the country the abbreviation stands for.

clue.text: Some screed I tediously corrected

indicators.note: some means a portion, so the answer is a run of letters within the next words

parts.note: a run of letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: Someone describes laboriously fixing a long-winded piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit text is to revise it and remove errors, so edited text has been corrected.

clue.text: I scorned corrupt judge

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or altered from its proper form, so the letters change order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to having spurned a bent magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider someone honest is to judge them so; both verbs mean to form an opinion or assessment.

clue.text: Disturb alien spaceship

parts.note: to rock is to shake or unsettle
ET is the extraterrestrial of Spielberg's film

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial craft unsettles the onlookers.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket is a vehicle propelled into space, so a spacecraft in general usage.

clue.text: Makes better kippers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: heals an illness or patient
second meaning: preserves fish by salting and smoking, as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: 'Kippers' looks like the noun for smoked herrings, but it is a verb here. A kipper is a split, salted, smoked herring, a British breakfast dish.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both heals a patient and preserves meat or fish by smoking, salting or drying.

clue.text: Help unhappy Cassie to accept Stan

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one set of letters receives the other inside it
an unhappy name is out of sorts, so its letters are put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A miserable Cassie needs help to come round to Stan, perhaps as a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistance is aid or support given to someone, a straightforward synonym for help as a noun.

clue.text: Sport in state of collapse

parts.note: RU is rugby union
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sporting organisation has fallen into disarray.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin is the condition of having fallen apart or been destroyed, a state of collapse.

clue.text: Leaders of avant-garde love unconventional media and theatre

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so the opening letters of the next words are kept

parts.note: opening letters of avant-garde and love

indicators.note: unconventional means not in the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Experimental artists enjoy alternative media and the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The Almeida is a London theatre in Islington known for adventurous new productions.
explanation.definitionFit: The Almeida is a well-known playhouse in north London, so a specific example of a theatre.

clue.text: Madonna, for example, has drinks with sailor

parts.note: pop is fizzy drink, plural here
a tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A singer is out drinking with a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: Madonna might be the Virgin Mary; here it is the singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Madonna is a hugely successful singer of chart music, the archetypal female celebrity of pop.
